newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition crisis dampens shares anew.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition crisis dampens shares anew.

text.p: Persistent doubts about the future of Turkey's Islamist-led coalition put fresh pressure on shares on Monday after a dissident parliamentarian warned of a possible new move to topple the government, brokers said.
Turkish economic data also disappointed the market.
The IMKB National-100 index ended the day down 3.33 percent, or 48 points at 1,395 after a late rebound, having hit a low of 1,381.

Political uncertainty, which has sliced eight percent off the value of stocks in under three weeks, kept many traders on the sidelines. Trading volume retreated to 7.11 trillion lira ($52.1 million) from 8.83 trillion on Friday.
"It is considered clear that the government will go. The economic data are not good either and because of that selling emerged," said Mursel Yildiz, a Vakifbank Securities broker.

A former minister from the Islamist-led coalition predicted efforts to bring down the shaky ruling alliance if his right-wing party did not support a new government formula set for discussion this week.
"If there is no resignation from the government, the government must be brought down with a confidence vote," former health minister Yildirim Aktuna from the True Path Party (DYP) said.

Another DYP dissident, former trade and industry minister Yalim Erez was to meet opposition leaders on Tuesday or Wednesday to discuss prospects for an alternative government excluding the Islamist Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
The two ministers quit because of Welfare's lack of commitment to military-led demands for the 10-month-old alliance to curb Islamist activism.

Negative sentiment in financial markets has been exacerbated by growing doubts over the government's ability to deliver on bold economic promises to accelerate privatisation and tackle shaky public finances, brokers said.
Erbakan, who announced a balanced budget plan late last year, acknowledged on Sunday the budget showed a deficit of more than $1 billion in March. .
The markets were also disappointed by a 4.7 percent rise in the trade deficit in the first quarter to $4.133 billion, over the same previous year period.
This came on the heels of inflation data showing a near 80 percent annual rise in April, brokers said.
They said from a political perspective a possible end to the coalition had been discounted by the share market in recent weeks, adding there was a limit to the downside in coming days.
Taksim Securities broker Erden Gokay said this view was supported by low volumes and the scale of recent declines.
"This may be a sign that we have come to the end of these declines. We may see a level of 1,350 points in the coming days, but I think at these levels we may begin a recovery," he said.
"There has to be an end to the uncertainty in politics for the market to move upwards," said Huseyin Istanbullu, a trader at Meksa Securities.
A recovery from the lower levels would depend heavily on how and when the political conflict was resolved, brokers said.
Monday's trading was led by largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli which fell 250 lira to 14,500, while new shares of bed manufacturer Yatas rose 1,000 lira to 12,500.
Bond yields firmed around 1.5 points in response to the political crisis, and in cautious trade ahead of a Treasury auction on Tuesday of two-year, inflation-indexed bonds.
($1=136,450 Turkish lira)
